description: INVOKE (OO method call), ISO §2023:14.9.23 — introduced 2002. THE EDGE IS QUOTED from the edition texts (kb/Work PB3965): COBOL-85 has no class or method, its Identification Division being 'IDENTIFICATION DIVISION. PROGRAM-ID. program-name.' (§1985:VI.3.2.1.1); 2002 adds 'The INVOKE statement causes a method to be invoked.' (§2002:14.8.22), §2002:F.1 item 6 lists INVOKE under 'Reserved words. The following reserved words have been added', and §2002:F.2 states the change, its item 82: 'Object orientation. Support for object oriented programming has been added.' 2014 keeps the statement (§2014:14.9.22) and makes object orientation optional, a feature 'required in the previous COBOL standard' (§2014:E.2 item 23: 'Required features made optional. A number of required features in the previous COBOL standard have been made optional', its list naming 'A.4.9, Object orientation'); §2023:14.9.23.1 carries the 2002 sentence. LIVE since the Phase-3 spine part 2 (DEVLOG 601): Class NEW RETURNING → new C(); no-arg instance INVOKE → virtual call behind the EC-OO-NULL guard (§2023:14.9.23.4 GR5); USING/RETURNING marshaling (slice 2), SELF/SUPER (3b), factory and universal dispatch stage loud. Below 2002 the VersionConformancePass parse arm names the edition on RECOGNITION (VisitInvokeStatement -> 0900) — invokeStatement carries no version predicate, so an INVOKE whose target does not resolve names its edition too (kb/Work PB353).

IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
PROGRAM-ID. IV.
ENVIRONMENT DIVISION.
CONFIGURATION SECTION.
REPOSITORY.
    CLASS IVC.
DATA DIVISION.
WORKING-STORAGE SECTION.
01 OBJ USAGE OBJECT REFERENCE IVC.
PROCEDURE DIVISION.
MAIN.
    INVOKE IVC "NEW" RETURNING OBJ.
    INVOKE OBJ "DOIT".
    STOP RUN.
END PROGRAM IV.

IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
CLASS-ID. IVC INHERITS FROM BASE.
ENVIRONMENT DIVISION.
CONFIGURATION SECTION.
REPOSITORY.
    CLASS BASE.
IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
OBJECT.
PROCEDURE DIVISION.
METHOD-ID. DOIT.
PROCEDURE DIVISION.
MAIN.
    DISPLAY "OK".
END METHOD DOIT.
END OBJECT.
END CLASS IVC.
